summary: John Taber is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding positions at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he served at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (1858–1861), and as Teacher of Persian at Oxford from 1880.

John Vincent Bellezza is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held an affiliation at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

John W. Pettit is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, while also studying under Dilgo Khyentse (1985–1990) and Ashok Gangadean.

John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Oregon under Don Levi, teaching there (1993–1994) before holding posts at the College of Wooster (1994–1995) and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).
John W. Spellman was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

John Wilson was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

John Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888) and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He served as a Calcutta High Court Judge (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).

Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Sadatomo Chihaya. He served as head of Hōryū-ji (1903–1950), joined the Imperial Academy (1929), and held posts at Horyu-ji Kangakuin and the University of Tokyo.
Joji Fujii is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1966–1974) and later held an academic post there (~1989–2011).

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1943–1948) and Kyoto University. He served as professor at Otemae University (~1966–1994) and held a post at Shuchiin University.

Jon Kabat-Zinn is a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College and MIT (Ph.D. ~1965–1971). He held posts at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (~1979–2000), UMass Memorial Medical Center, and the Insight Meditation Society.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford (D.Phil. ~1989–1994 under Bimal Krishna Matilal). His posts include the University of Nottingham (~1997–2004), Sussex (~2008–2013), Monash (~2013–2015), NYU (~2013–2020), and Toronto (~2020).

Jonathan A. Silk works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Oberlin and the University of Michigan (PhD ~1994 under Luis Oscar Gómez), later holding posts at Western Michigan University, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University (Director, 2007).

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and taught as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff, later teaching at McMaster, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1963). He served as fellow and tutor in philosophy at New College (~1967–1996) and held posts at King's College London (~1996–2013) and Oxford.

Jonathan Lear is a philosopher educated at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (Ph.D. ~1973–1978). He held academic posts at Yale (1978–1996), the University of Cambridge and Clare College (~1978–1985), and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1970–1983), he was appointed professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1985).
